_meta.schema: Same contract as incentive_canon.json. Read jurisdictions[] by code or country+region, gate on has_program, prefill from headline_pct. headline_pct = null means DO NOT PREFILL — a published rate exists but cannot currently be drawn; published_pct still carries the figure for display. '[UNRESOLVED]' in notes marks a value where sources conflict, and conflicts[] carries the detail. verified_on is the OLDER of the row's own verification and the last time any source behind it was opened.
_meta.watcher_status: NEVER RUN. Last_Checked and Last_Result are empty on 114 of 114 source rows. The Sources tab calls itself 'the input to the Apps Script watcher'; that watcher does not exist. Freshness here is manual and the dates say when a human last looked.

Grants up to the stated ceiling cover up to 80% of documented costs; larger support is available only as a loan.

Foreign cast and crew qualify only where remuneration is taxed in Hungary, which requires a double-taxation treaty. Remuneration is eligible at 100% to HUF 3M per person and 50% above; the taper does not apply to Hungarian self-employed or loan-out personnel taxed outside personal income tax. NFI deducts a 2.5% administration fee. Producer fees capped at 4%, completion bond at 5% of budget to a HUF 100M ceiling. Invoices dated more than 3 months after the production end date are excluded.

The Maximum requires ALL THREE of: at least ISK 350M of Icelandic production costs; at least 30 working days in Iceland of which a minimum of 10 are shooting days; and at least 50 staff working directly on the project totalling at least 50 working days. Salary and payments to employees and contractors must be taxed in Iceland. Where more than 80% of total production cost is incurred in Iceland, reimbursement is calculated on total cost across the EEA, Greenland and the Faroe Islands.

Credit is 32% of the LOWEST of eligible Irish expenditure, 80% of total production cost, or the per-project cap. Total production cost must be at least EUR 250,000. TWO SEPARATE ROUTES TO 40%. VFX route: spend at least EUR 1M on Irish VFX and the whole Irish spend earns 40% on the first EUR 10M, reverting to 32% above it. Sceal route: features under EUR 20M total qualifying expenditure, needing an Irish or EEA national in a key creative role and 5 days theatrical release in Ireland.
Non-repayable and VAT-exempt.
Lazio Cinema International is the international co-production line, funded through PR FESR Lazio 2021-2027. No rate or per-project ceiling published.

Rates shown are net of corporation tax; gross rates are 34% standard and 39% VFX. Qualifying UK core spend is the LOWER of actual UK core spend or 80% of total core expenditure - but UK VFX spend is EXEMPT from that cap, so the Maximum carries a double benefit. THE VFX RATE IS ONLY PAID AT FINAL CERTIFICATE; interim claims pay the standard rate on VFX costs and remain subject to the 80% cap. Minimum UK core spend is 10% of total core expenditure, a percentage rather than a cash floor. Animated features take the 29.25% net rate on all core spend. IFTC pays 39.75% net but only for films with core expenditure under GBP 23.5M, with the cash credit capped at GBP 4.77M net, and IFTC films cannot claim the VFX rate. No cap on the amount claimable under standard AVEC. Legacy Film Tax Relief closes 1 Apr 2027.
AVEC is UK-wide - a production here claims the same net rate as one in London and nothing more. NI Screen production funding is a recoupable award with profit participation.
